name: Monarchism
summary: Monarchism holds that a hereditary monarch is the best or a legitimate head of state. Its classical defenders (Bodin, Filmer, James VI and I, Bossuet) ground royal power in paternal and divine authority and deny any right of resistance; counter-revolutionary and traditionalist writers (Maistre, Maurras, the Carlists) defend throne and altar, organic institutions and inherited legitimacy against popular sovereignty; and constitutional monarchists (Bagehot, Hegel, modern monarchist leagues) defend a crown above party that gives continuity and unity while elected ministers govern. It is mainly a doctrine about the form of the state and says little about economic policy.
scope: Monarchism as the advocacy of hereditary monarchy, covering both its absolutist and divine-right strand (Bodin, Filmer, James VI and I, Bossuet), its counter-revolutionary and traditionalist strand (Maistre, Maurras's Action française, Spanish Carlism) and its modern constitutional strand (Bagehot, Hegel's constitutional monarchy, the Monarchist League of Canada and International Monarchist League). Answers rest on what these texts state; where strands split (sovereign above law, parliament, resistance, democracy, separation of powers) the answer is 0 or a weak lean at low confidence. Economic and most social questions are not addressed by monarchism as such and are low. Excludes specific national royalist parties' wider platforms and anarcho-capitalist arguments that monarchy is merely a lesser evil (Hoppe).

keyFigures.name: Jacques-Bénigne Bossuet
keyFigures.role: Theorist of sacred, paternal and absolute royal authority under Louis XIV.

keyFigures.name: Joseph de Maistre
keyFigures.role: Counter-revolutionary defender of hereditary monarchy, throne and altar.

keyFigures.name: Walter Bagehot
keyFigures.role: Author of The English Constitution, the classic case for a constitutional crown above party.

sources.title: Monarchism
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.usedFor: Overview of arguments for monarchy (Bogdanor, Feeney, Orwell, Hobbes, Kuehnelt-Leddihn, Hoppe, Otto von Habsburg), types of monarchy and modern movements.

sources.title: The English Constitution
sources.author: Walter Bagehot
sources.usedFor: Monarchy as intelligible and dignified government, religious sanction, crown of no party, the rights to be consulted, encourage and warn, deference, the Lords, fear of the new electorate.

sources.title: Considerations on France (excerpt)
sources.author: Joseph de Maistre
sources.usedFor: Regicide as a national crime, the Revolution as an antireligious insurrection and providential punishment, the most Christian king.

sources.title: Constitutional monarchy
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.usedFor: Modern crowns acting on ministerial advice, reserve powers, symbol of unity, armed forces' allegiance to the Crown, executive versus ceremonial monarchies.

sources.title: Patriarcha (excerpts)
sources.author: Sir Robert Filmer
sources.usedFor: Royal authority derived from fatherly power, rejection of natural liberty and popular choice of rulers, king not bound by positive law, no remedy for subjects against rulers.

sources.title: The True Law of Free Monarchies (excerpt)
sources.author: James VI and I
sources.usedFor: King prior to parliaments and laws, king above the law as its author, parliament as the king's head court, good king conforming to law, king as overlord of the land.

sources.title: Writings and speeches of James I (excerpts)
sources.author: James VI and I
sources.usedFor: Kings as God's lieutenants and fathers of their people, sedition of disputing royal power, a just prince taking no life without law.

sources.title: Politics Drawn from the Very Words of Holy Scripture (excerpt)
sources.author: Jacques-Bénigne Bossuet
sources.usedFor: Royal authority sacred, paternal and absolute but not arbitrary, accountable to God alone, given for the good of the people, religion and royal authority bound together.

sources.title: Jean Bodin
sources.author: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy
sources.usedFor: Sovereignty as absolute and perpetual power bound by natural and divine law, ban on tyrannicide against a lawful sovereign, provisional toleration, crown lands, money.

sources.title: Philosophy of Right: The Constitution (internal side), §§272-320
sources.author: G. W. F. Hegel
sources.usedFor: Constitutional monarchy as the achievement of the modern world, hereditary monarch by birth, elective monarchy the worst institution, critique of popular sovereignty, ministers answerable.

sources.title: Philosophy of Right: External sovereignty, §§321-329
sources.author: G. W. F. Hegel
sources.usedFor: The crown commands the armed forces and conducts war, peace and diplomacy; peoples more excitable than monarchs.

sources.title: Enquête sur la monarchie, preface to the 1909 edition, III
sources.author: Charles Maurras
sources.usedFor: Royalism argued from national salvation, the nation as the highest political frame, national questions not settled by vote.

sources.title: Enquête sur la monarchie, Discours préliminaire, VII
sources.author: Charles Maurras
sources.usedFor: Liberal and parliamentary anarchy, parties and the press turned against the nation, the public as an ignorant crowd, antisemitic charges.

sources.title: Enquête sur la monarchie (table of contents)
sources.author: Charles Maurras
sources.usedFor: Structure of the argument: rejection of parliamentary monarchy, decentralisation, the pays of France, associations, royalist dictatorship.

sources.title: Liberty or Equality: The Challenge of Our Time (book page)
sources.author: Mises Institute, on Erik von Kuehnelt-Leddihn
sources.usedFor: Kuehnelt-Leddihn's thesis that democratic equality leads to the total state and that monarchy restrained by aristocracy upheld liberty.

sources.title: Spanish Carlism: An Introduction
sources.author: Miguel Ayuso
sources.usedFor: Carlist traditional monarchy: Catholic unity, fueros and subsidiarity, a king bound by God and by the rights of bodies, legitimacy by birth and conduct, rejection of liberal constitutionalism.

sources.title: Who We Are
sources.author: Monarchist League of Canada
sources.usedFor: Modern constitutional-monarchist case: Crown free of partisan bickering, pillar of parliamentary democracy, inclusive symbol of identity and heritage.

sources.title: Joseph de Maistre
sources.author: New World Encyclopedia
sources.usedFor: Maistre's view of institutions as matured by God, hereditary monarchy, papal supremacy, established Catholicism, anti-rationalism.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Monarchism is a form-of-government doctrine with no healthcare position; royalist parties range from paternalist to free-market.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Nothing in monarchist sources addresses wage law, and monarchists divide along ordinary left-right lines on it.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Hoppe argues for monarchy on market-liberty grounds but traditionalist monarchists favour paternalist order, so adherents split.

public-ownership.rationale: Crown estates and royal monopolies existed historically, but no doctrine prescribes public ownership of utilities; adherents are split.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Not a monarchist question; noblesse-oblige monarchists and propertied royalists would answer oppositely.

unions-good.rationale: Monarchists historically preferred guild-like or organic bodies, yet the doctrine is silent on modern unions; inferred and split.

property-fundamental.rationale: Bodin treated crown lands as the people's property and resisted their alienation, and Kuehnelt-Leddihn's monarchism is allied with classical liberty, but James VI and I made the king overlord of all land; lean agree, low.

regulate-corporations.rationale: No source ties monarchism to corporate regulation, and paternalist and laissez-faire royalists disagree.

cut-welfare.rationale: The doctrine is silent on welfare; noblesse-oblige tradition favours care for the poor while some royalists are fiscal conservatives.

worker-ownership.rationale: Worker ownership is a socialist programme alien to hierarchical, hereditary order; inferred, not documented.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Monarchist sources do not discuss surveillance, and security-minded and libertarian royalists differ.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Traditionalist monarchists lean towards moral order and restriction, though this is inference and libertarian monarchists differ.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: No monarchist doctrine on speech law; adherents range from libertarian to traditionalist.

strong-leader.rationale: Constitutional monarchists want a symbolic crown above politics, not a leader bypassing gridlock, while absolutists welcome one; the strands split.

state-harmful.rationale: Monarchism is a defence of a particular state form; Hegel says that without its monarch and organised structure a people is a formless mass, not a state.

limit-guns.rationale: Gun law is not a monarchist issue; adherents in different countries answer differently.

empower-police-military.rationale: Monarchies treat the armed forces as owing allegiance to the Crown, and royalists are generally order-minded, but funding is not a doctrinal matter.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Traditionalist monarchists tend towards moral conservatism; inferred, with libertarian monarchists dissenting.

decide-locally.rationale: Maurras argues the Republic is unable to decentralise and the Carlists defended regional fueros as a form of subsidiarity, but absolutist and centralising monarchies did the opposite, so the lean is to agree with low confidence.

rehabilitation.rationale: No monarchist doctrine on punishment philosophy; royal prerogative of mercy exists but adherents split.

traditional-family.rationale: Filmer and Bossuet model royal authority on the father's authority in the family, and Bagehot argues a family on the throne makes the state humanly intelligible.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Traditionalist and religious monarchists tend to oppose, though many modern constitutional royalists accept it; contested and inferred.

abortion-legal.rationale: Religious-traditionalist monarchists lean pro-life, but this is not doctrine and secular royalists differ.

more-religion-public.rationale: Bossuet says the service of God and respect for kings are bound together, Maistre treats the Revolution as an antireligious revolt, and Bagehot says the monarchy strengthens government with the strength of religion.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Not addressed in monarchist sources; adherents split by wider politics.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Inferred from hierarchy-and-nature thinking of Kuehnelt-Leddihn and Lewis; not a stated monarchist doctrine.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Maurras makes the nation the highest political frame and the Monarchist League of Canada presents royal symbols as an essential part of national identity and heritage.

gradual-change.rationale: Maistre holds that constitutions are matured by God over time rather than designed, and Bagehot defends institutions by the reverence that long continuity gives them; abrupt rational redesign is what both reject.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Immigration is not a monarchist issue; royalist parties vary from restrictionist to liberal.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Monarchism upholds a national crown and sovereignty; inferred, though the EU-era Habsburg tradition (von Habsburg) was more pro-integration.

free-trade.rationale: No doctrine on trade; mercantilist absolutists and free-market royalists differ.

nation-first.rationale: The crown symbolises national identity, but nothing in sources commits monarchists to putting national interest above cooperation.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Monarchist sources are silent on this; adherents split.

open-borders.rationale: A crown tied to a nation and territory sits poorly with open borders, inferred rather than documented.

limit-growth.rationale: No monarchist doctrine on degrowth, and conservative royalists generally resist it; inferred.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Not addressed; some royals advocate environmentalism while many royalists are sceptical of drastic state action.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Monarchism is about institutional form and takes no stance on techno-optimism.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Energy policy lies outside monarchist doctrine.

revolution-justified.rationale: Maistre calls the French Revolution an antireligious and antisocial insurrection and the king's killing a national crime, and James VI and I calls disputing royal power sedition.

experts-over-public.rationale: Hegel has counsellors supply the substance of decisions, Bagehot praises a deferential electorate guided by the educated, and Maurras says national questions are not for a vote; this is drawn from their views of government rather than a stated position on experts, so it is low.

central-planning.rationale: No monarchist doctrine on economic planning; royalists are mostly conservative and sceptical, though absolutist states practised mercantilism.

socialized-markets.rationale: Economic ownership is not addressed by monarchism.

land-value-tax.rationale: Fiscal technique is outside monarchist doctrine.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Hereditary succession is core to monarchism, so adherents tend to defend inheritance; inferred.

basic-income.rationale: Welfare design is not a monarchist question.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Trade policy is not monarchist doctrine; adherents split.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Not addressed; historical monarchies did direct investment but modern royalists differ.

widespread-small-property.rationale: No doctrine on property distribution; landed-aristocracy royalists differ from distributist ones.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Abolishing money is a communist aim that monarchists reject as incompatible with inherited order; inferred.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Monetary institutions are outside monarchist doctrine.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Corporatist and guild ideas appeal to some traditionalist monarchists, but modern constitutional royalists do not hold them as doctrine.

one-party-rule.rationale: Monarchists want a head of state above party, as Bagehot's crown of no party and the Monarchist League's non-partisan Crown show, not rule by one ideological party.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Every source defends hereditary monarchy: Hegel calls birth and inheritance the basis of the crown's legitimacy, Bagehot calls monarchy the strongest because most intelligible government, and Filmer derives kingship from paternal power.

democracy-best.rationale: Kuehnelt-Leddihn argues democratic equality leads to the total state, Hegel calls the people without a monarch a formless mass and Maurras blames parliamentary anarchy, but constitutional monarchists like the Monarchist League treat the Crown as a pillar of parliamentary democracy, so the strands are split.

direct-votes.rationale: Monarchists generally favour representative or mixed institutions under a crown over plebiscitary rule; inferred from their distrust of mob rule.

workers-councils.rationale: Councils as the basis of power replace the crown and parliament with a revolutionary form; monarchists reject it.

right-to-secede.rationale: A crown unifying a multinational state, as Bogdanor says of Belgium, implies attachment to the realm's integrity; not stated as doctrine.

natural-rulers.rationale: Filmer rejects natural equality and freedom from subjection, Kuehnelt-Leddihn credits a noble elite with restraining power, and Bagehot values deference to the better educated.

political-violence-never.rationale: Maistre justifies violence by the state and punishment, and monarchists defend wars and force by the crown; but they condemn revolutionary violence.

war-builds-character.rationale: Not a monarchist doctrine; martial absolutists and peaceable constitutionalists differ.

separate-church-state.rationale: Throne-and-altar monarchists such as Bossuet and Maistre join royal authority to the church, and Ayuso's Carlism rejects secular constitutionalism; constitutional monarchists keep a looser link, so disagree rather than strongly.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Divine-right monarchists like Bossuet drew politics from scripture, but modern constitutional monarchists do not; the strands split.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Hoppe is a libertarian exception, but the crown traditionally embodies the state's justice and defence; the mainstream rejects privatising them.

military-superiority.rationale: Royalists tend to be security-minded and the armed forces owe allegiance to the Crown, but no doctrine demands superiority.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Monarchists praise the crown for uniting multiethnic states (Belgium, UK per Bogdanor), yet nationalist royalists exist; split.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Bagehot and later monarchists present the crown as a unifier of society, and the Marxist claim of class conflict as the main driver is rejected.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Kuehnelt-Leddihn argued that humans are naturally unequal and that pursuit of equality by abolishing monarchy reduces liberty, so enforced equal outcomes are rejected.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Miskito and tribal kingship show some monarchism within indigenous traditions, but there is no general doctrine.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Inferred from imperial and conservative royalism; not addressed in sources.

civilizational-union.rationale: Habsburg-style supranational royalism exists but no general doctrine; split.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Traditional monarchist ethics stress loyalty, duty and honour over self-interest; inferred.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Monarchist tradition stresses loyalty and duty to crown and community, and Maistre opposes the Revolution's individual rights; mainstream constitutional royalists accept rights, so only moderately.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Some traditionalists lament modernity, but monarchism as such does not call industrial civilization a disaster; inferred.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Monarchism prizes continuity and inherited institutions over disruption, so it resists disruptive acceleration; inferred.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Government by a personal sovereign and tradition conflicts with algorithmic rule; inferred.

restore-past-order.rationale: Maistre sought a Bourbon restoration and the International Monarchist League works to restore crowns in republics; constitutional monarchists in existing realms aim to preserve rather than restore.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Monarchists praise pragmatic continuity, yet doctrinal royalists argue on principle; split.

direct-action.rationale: Monarchists work through crown, parliament and parties; direct action is more a revolutionary tactic, inferred.

means-match-ends.rationale: Monarchist sources do not discuss the link between methods and ends; restorationists and reformers differ.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Primitivism rejects state and hierarchy altogether; monarchism cannot accept it.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Hierarchical order of ranks and functions is the monarchist background; inferred.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Communist principle, opposed to hierarchical inherited order; inferred.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Marxist exploitation theory presumes class conflict that monarchists reject in favour of social unity under the crown.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: A class dictatorship replacing the crown is the opposite of a hereditary, non-party head of state; monarchist writers oppose revolutionary rule of any class.

collective-farming.rationale: Collective farming is communist policy opposed to landed order and private holdings; inferred.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist thesis that monarchists do not hold; inferred.

taxation-theft.rationale: Only libertarian monarchists like Hoppe come close; the mainstream accepts the crown's right to tax.

harm-principle.rationale: Liberal principle; traditionalist monarchists accept moral legislation while liberal royalists accept the harm principle.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Maistre attacked the Revolution's rights doctrine, and monarchists value community bodies such as church and crown; modern constitutional royalists accept individual rights too.

conscription.rationale: Armed forces owe allegiance to the crown but conscription itself is not a monarchist position.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Mostly libertarian royalists like Hoppe argue for exit, but the mainstream defends loyalty to the realm; inferred.

state-as-business.rationale: Hobbes saw the monarch's interest as aligned with subjects' wealth, but nobody equates citizens with customers; inferred disagreement.

positive-liberty.rationale: The monarchist sources discuss liberty only as protected by the crown (Kuehnelt-Leddihn, Hoppe), not as material means; adherents are split.

media-academia-power.rationale: Conservative royalists often voice this view but monarchism as doctrine does not.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Not a monarchist doctrine; mainstream monarchists treat dynastic descent not race as basis, inferred.

organic-representation.rationale: Traditionalist monarchists favour representation through regions, bodies and associations rather than parties (Maurras on associations and the pays, Carlist fueros), while modern constitutional monarchists work through party parliaments, so strands are split.

total-state.rationale: Constitutional monarchy limits state power by constitution and custom; Kuehnelt-Leddihn argued monarchies are freer than republics.

national-rebirth.rationale: Restorationist royalists speak of renewal, while constitutional ones prize continuity; split.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Historic monarchies expanded, but modern constitutional royalists do not advocate it.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Feudal personal-oath rule belongs to medieval monarchism; modern monarchists do not demand it.

bound-labor.rationale: Serfdom is a feudal institution that no modern monarchist movement promotes; inferred.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Maistre-style traditionalism asserts providential truth and universal moral order; inferred.

universal-morality.rationale: Bodin binds even the absolute sovereign by natural and divine law, and Maistre and Bossuet ground politics in a moral order set by God.

single-common-good.rationale: Bagehot's crown of no party and Hegel's monarch as the single point of decision for the whole state express rule for one common good above faction.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Not addressed by monarchism; adherents split.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Monarchism takes no position on citizenship for diasporas, though exiled dynasties have sometimes sought return themselves.

revive-national-language.rationale: Language revival is a nationalist cause that monarchist sources never address, so adherents are split.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Democratic control of firms is a left proposal; monarchism's hierarchical bent gives mild disagreement.

school-vouchers.rationale: Education finance is outside monarchist doctrine.

economic-freedom.rationale: Hoppe ties monarchy to liberty but traditionalists do not make economic freedom a condition; split.

rule-by-example.rationale: James VI and I says a good king should follow the law to set an example to his subjects, but Bagehot warns royal virtue cannot be counted on, so the lean is mild and low.

national-self-determination.rationale: Monarchists support realms and dynasties, which sometimes ran against national self-determination (Habsburg multinational empire).

force-without-un.rationale: The sources say nothing about UN authorisation; royalists divide as other conservatives and liberals do on foreign force.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Maistre attacked Enlightenment rationalism and scientism and grounded institutions in providence, and Bossuet in Scripture.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Welfare eligibility is outside monarchist doctrine and royalist parties differ on it.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Workfare is a welfare-policy question that monarchist sources never discuss; adherents split.

class-collaboration.rationale: Bagehot says the monarchy gives society a shared focus of reverence and the crown is claimed to unite classes, so adherents favour cooperation over struggle.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Monarchists value inherited institutions and heritage, as Feeney's entrenched customs argument shows.

dominated-front.rationale: A common front against the West is a third-world nationalist idea not found in the monarchist sources; adherents divide.

workers-nation.rationale: Not addressed; royalists would favour national over class framing.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Traditionalist royalists lean yes while modern constitutional monarchies have gender-neutral succession; split.

ban-interest.rationale: Usury bans belong to medieval religious tradition; modern monarchists do not push them.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Monarchism is not a racial doctrine; monarchs rule across ethnic groups and Bogdanor praises the crown for representing all citizens.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Bagehot presents the crown as a dignified, unifying institution and monarchists reject the Marxist theory that the state serves one class.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Not addressed; nationalist royalists lean yes, multicultural constitutional monarchies differ.

elite-replacement.rationale: Great Replacement theory is a conspiracy claim not part of monarchism; inferred.

proportional-representation.rationale: Electoral systems under a crown are not addressed.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Inferred from hierarchy-and-nature thinking; no source states it.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Monarchists often criticise politicians, as Feeney's populist-check argument implies, but it is not doctrine.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Eugenic policy is not part of monarchism and religious royalists oppose it; inferred.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Accountability for past security-force abuses is not addressed in monarchist doctrine, and royalists with ties to the armed forces differ.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Hoppe-style royalists accept it, but traditional monarchies exercised broad powers; split.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Dynasties historically intermarried across nations and monarchism has no racial doctrine.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Monarchists hold human beings equal before God per Maistre's Christian frame, yet defend hereditary rank and natural inequality (Kuehnelt-Leddihn), so adherents are split.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: The question of settler colonialism is not covered by monarchist sources; Commonwealth royalists and others would differ.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Monarchism has no stance on uniform versus religious personal law; royalists in different states answer differently.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Not addressed; depends on state faith.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Cattle slaughter law belongs to Hindu-nationalist politics, not monarchist doctrine, so adherents are split.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Monarchies with established churches often keep religion in schools; inferred.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Filmer calls the idea that people are born free to choose their rulers dangerous and unscriptural, and Hegel dismisses popular sovereignty as a confused notion; constitutional monarchists accept elected government but locate the Crown's authority in inheritance rather than consent.

trade-surplus.rationale: Mercantilist absolutist states favoured it but modern royalists are indifferent.

population-transfer.rationale: No monarchist doctrine; monarchs rule multiethnic states per Bogdanor; inferred.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Monarchy rests on state authority and hereditary power, so absolute non-aggression is not endorsed (Hoppe aside).

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Monarchist sources praise continuity and unity more than struggle, but none address progress through competition, so adherents are split.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Orwell credited monarchy with preventing extremism and constitutional royalists generally defend the constitutional order; inferred.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Republican theory of freedom is the rival tradition to monarchism; inferred disagreement though monarchists claim liberty too.

separated-powers.rationale: Bodin's sovereignty is indivisible and Bagehot describes the British system as a fusion of executive and legislature, while Hegel and constitutional monarchists value differentiated powers with ministers answerable; the strands are split.

vanguard-party.rationale: A disciplined revolutionary party leading the working class is opposed to monarchism and the crown above parties.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Noblesse oblige suggests care for the poor but it is not stated as doctrine.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Strike law is a labour-policy question outside the monarchist sources; adherents divide along ordinary party lines.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: The Malthusian thesis is not part of monarchism; sources never raise it and adherents are split.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Monarchists argue the crown unifies diverse nations (Bogdanor on Belgium), implying diversity can be bridged; inferred.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Hereditary and appointed offices are the monarchist norm; lottery is a radical-democratic idea; inferred.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Reserve powers exist for emergencies and some royalists welcome them, but constitutional royalists stress legality; split.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Historic crowns often controlled grain prices, but modern monarchism holds no position on price controls.

party-controls-media.rationale: Single-party media control conflicts with the crown standing above parties and with Kuehnelt-Leddihn's claim that monarchies are freer; inferred.

party-commands-army.rationale: In monarchist doctrine the armed forces belong to the crown and the state, not to a party: Hegel gives command of the forces to the crown and modern realms' forces owe allegiance to the Crown.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Naturalisation rules are not covered by monarchist sources; adherents divide as other conservatives and liberals do.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Monarchists do not hold such democratic-egalitarian pay demands; inferred.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Monarchists value a crown above party and independent representatives; inferred.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Habsburg-circle royalism favoured integration, while sovereigntist royalists oppose; split.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Hegel gives the crown command of the armed forces and the conduct of war and diplomacy, and in modern realms the forces owe allegiance to the Crown and ministers are appointed in its name, though usually on advice.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Depends on national church; Anglican and Catholic royalists agree, Presbyterian ones do not.

clerical-rule.rationale: Maistre sought alliance of throne and altar, not rule by clergy, and monarchists place the crown highest.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Defeatism is a Leninist stance contrary to loyalty to the crown and realm; inferred.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Not addressed; traditionalists lean yes while liberal royalists lean no.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Re-election is a republican issue; monarchs serve for life.

recall-officials.rationale: Recall is a direct-democracy device; monarchists favour stable tenure; inferred.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Monarchies join alliances like NATO; no doctrine, inferred.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: A radical-egalitarian proposal opposed to propertied order; inferred.

people-in-arms.rationale: The crown commands a standing professional army in monarchist states; inferred.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Landed traditionalists lean yes but not doctrine.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Monarchists neither endorse nor reject reunification as such; it depends on which dynasty or state is involved.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Royalist writers distrust some elites, but the sources never single out the university-educated, so adherents are split.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Traditionalists tend to prize their own civilization, yet doctrine is silent.

death-penalty.rationale: Monarchs historically had this power but modern monarchies abolished it; adherents split.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Sex education is not addressed in monarchist sources; religious traditionalists oppose it and secular royalists accept it.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Dynastic descent governs succession but citizenship law is not addressed.

minority-language-support.rationale: Multinational crowns such as Belgium's accommodate languages, but doctrine does not require support.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Exemptions for religious minorities are not covered by monarchist sources, and established-church royalists and pluralists differ.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Mill's liberal claim; traditionalist monarchists defend custom, inferred.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Debt relief is outside monarchist doctrine; royalists in creditor and debtor states would answer differently.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Left anticolonial view; royalism does not tie politics to property systems; inferred.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Maistre held that constitutions grow from history and providence and cannot be written by assemblies, and Carlists rejected the Cadiz constitution's popular sovereignty.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Not addressed; absolutists yes, constitutionalists no.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Noblesse oblige might suggest a duty of aid, but the sources apply it to individuals, not states, so adherents are split.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Deterrence policy is not monarchist doctrine; royalists in Britain and France versus other states answer differently.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Bagehot argues that an elected head chosen to pick ministers would in practice be a partisan figure, and Hegel rejects election of the head of state outright; monarchists want the office filled by birth, not by any vote.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Territorial concessions are not covered by monarchist sources, and adherents divide according to the national case.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Noblesse-oblige royalists agree while propertied ones disagree; not addressed in sources.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Environmental regulation is outside monarchist doctrine; some royals champion green causes while others favour caution about state action.

collective-defense.rationale: Monarchies are in NATO but doctrine is silent.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Monarchism as a doctrine does not address annexation law, and royalists differ with each dispute.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Absolutist crowns curbed the church while throne-and-altar royalists like Maistre allied with it; split.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Bagehot says the nation is divided into parties but the crown is of no party, and the Monarchist League of Canada presents the Crown as free from political bickering and ambition.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Not addressed; royalists defend realm unity but doctrine is silent on force.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Not addressed; composite monarchies historically allowed it.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Bossuet holds the king's person sacred and James says kings are called gods, but none claims divine descent and constitutional monarchists treat the sacred aura only as useful sentiment (Bagehot), so on the full statement the strands are split.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Tax structure is not addressed in monarchist sources, and royalists are split between flat-tax conservatives and progressive-tax paternalists.

character-from-environment.rationale: Hereditary monarchy presumes inherited fitness and breeding of a dynasty, which implies innate nature matters; inferred.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Bodin, Filmer and James VI and I hold the sovereign free of the positive laws he or his predecessors made, while constitutional monarchists and Carlist traditionalists bind the king by law and by the rights of bodies, so the strands are split.

space-expansion.rationale: Space policy is never addressed by monarchist sources; adherents have no common view.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Constitutional monarchists defend crown, lords and commons together, while absolutists like Bodin and Filmer place undivided sovereignty in the king; the strands are split.

leader-cult.rationale: Monarchs are honoured through portraits and ceremony, but royalists distinguish this from partisan cults of personality; Thai lese majeste shows the extreme.

equal-parenting.rationale: Custody law is not part of monarchist doctrine; adherents divide between traditional and reformist views.

land-redistribution.rationale: Seizing landed estates is a revolutionary measure that monarchists, who defend inherited property and aristocracy, oppose.

refugee-return.rationale: Return of refugees and their descendants is not covered by monarchist sources, though exiled dynasties have claimed their own return.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Territorial claims on co-nationals abroad are not monarchist doctrine, and the Habsburg and Hohenzollern tradition gives mixed guidance.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Only some religious absolute monarchies do this; mainstream monarchism does not address it.

women-must-cover.rationale: Applies to a few Islamic monarchies but is not monarchist doctrine and most monarchists would reject it; inferred.

common-currency.rationale: Monetary union is not addressed in monarchist sources; Habsburg-circle integrationists and sovereigntist royalists differ.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Pan-national unions are not monarchist doctrine, and historic dynastic states were often multi-ethnic rather than kin-based.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Habsburg-style royalism favoured it, but doctrine is silent.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: The sources do not address strategies for persecuted minorities; this is a nationalist-movement debate, not a monarchist one.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Monarchist tradition stresses providence, ideas, custom and personal rulers over economic determinism; Maistre reads history providentially.

ban-cartels.rationale: Competition law is outside monarchist doctrine; royalists divide between market liberals and traditional paternalists.

no-bailouts.rationale: Bailout policy is not discussed in monarchist sources, and adherents divide along ordinary economic lines.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Constitutional monarchy stresses constitutional limits and judicial independence under law, which royalists value as checks against populism (Feeney).

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Mandated parity runs against hierarchy and tradition; inferred.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Autarkic imperial blocs were fascist-era policy, not part of monarchist doctrine, so the sources give no view and adherents are split.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Trade-agreement standards are not covered by monarchist sources; adherents split.

moral-incentives.rationale: Moral rather than material incentives is a socialist-planning idea absent from monarchist sources; adherents are split.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Maistre calls revolution a crime and monarchists defend the established crown against insurrection.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Kuehnelt-Leddihn argues that monarchy restrained by a hereditary nobility, not democracy, gave Europe its liberty, and Hegel grounds the crown itself in birth and inheritance, so abolishing hereditary standing strikes at the core.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Royalists value national tradition and the crown as embodiment of national continuity (Feeney, Hegel), implying a national-centred curriculum; inferred.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Imperial monarchies justified it historically, but modern monarchists do not hold it as doctrine.

patriotic-education.rationale: Loyalty to crown, flag and nation is central to monarchist culture, and the crown is presented as the focus of national unity (Bogdanor), though schools are not discussed directly.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Not addressed; adherents split by wider politics.

public-money-creation.rationale: Monetary reform is not addressed by monarchist doctrine, and royalists hold no common position.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: The sources are silent on capitalism's crises, and adherents divide with wider political leanings.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Influence over former imperial lands is a foreign policy question that monarchist sources do not address; adherents are split.

delink-world-market.rationale: Dependency-school thesis not part of monarchism; inferred.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Libertarian royalists like Hoppe say yes, traditionalists do not; split.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Constitutional royalists accept written limits but British-tradition royalists rely on custom; split.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: The status of colonial-era treaties is not addressed in monarchist sources, and imperial and anti-colonial royalists would differ.

elective-rulers.rationale: Hegel writes that elective monarchy is the worst of institutions because it hands the final decision to particular wills and turns offices into private property.

minority-veto.rationale: A veto for any member contradicts monarchist authority and unity under a crown; inferred.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Filmer allows subjects no remedy against unjust rule, Bossuet makes the king accountable to God alone and Bodin forbids tyrannicide against a lawful sovereign; the 1688 constitutional tradition accepts removal, so strands are split and the lean is against.

parliament-supreme.rationale: James VI and I makes parliament the king's court that cannot make law without him, and Maurras rejects parliamentary monarchy, while modern constitutional monarchists defend a Crown that reigns under parliament; the strands are split.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Animal ethics is not addressed in monarchist sources; adherents split.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Animal welfare is not a monarchist doctrinal issue, and rural traditionalist and urban royalists differ.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Filmer describes the king's office as a universal fatherly care of his people and Bossuet says royal power is given for the good of the people, with mercy toward the weak.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Monarchist tradition values service and loyalty to the realm; inferred.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: The critical-theory claim about mass culture is not a monarchist question; Lewis and Orwell comment on honouring celebrities but not in this way.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Bagehot sees reverence for the dignified crown as winning consent, but the Gramscian framing is not monarchist.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: World-systems theory is a left thesis not addressed by monarchist sources, so adherents are split.

native-born-offices.rationale: Not addressed; some monarchies reserve the throne by descent but doctrine is silent on offices.

party-own-road.rationale: The question concerns communist party relations, which monarchist sources never address.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Development strategy is not covered by monarchist doctrine; adherents have no common view.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Monarchism itself does not address irredentism, though restorationist royalists in some states have claimed lost lands.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Inferred; indigenous monarchies exist (Miskito kingship) but the doctrine does not support ethnic leadership claims.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Orwell credited monarchy with saving Britain from fascism, yet royalist parties like the DNVP backed restoration, so adherents split.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Orwell credited monarchy with protecting Britain from fascism, but the sources do not address condemning communism and fascism together, so adherents split.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: This is an American historical dispute that monarchist doctrine does not address.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Respect for inherited institutions and heritage points this way but the issue is not discussed.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Gender-policy attention is not addressed in monarchist sources, and adherents divide on it.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: The sources do not discuss domestic violence policy; adherents split.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Royalists defend their own tradition, but doctrine is silent on universal institutions; split between Western constitutional and Gulf absolute monarchists.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Monarchs command the forces and some crowns used the army as guardian (Thailand), but modern royalists differ.

paid-care-work.rationale: Payment for unpaid care work is outside monarchist doctrine, and royalists split between traditionalist and reformist views.

filial-duty.rationale: Hierarchy, loyalty and dynastic family tradition suggest it but it is not stated.

office-by-exam.rationale: Imperial Chinese-style exam selection is a bureaucratic practice not discussed in the monarchist sources; European monarchism relied on lineage and patronage, so adherents are split.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Investment screening is not addressed in monarchist sources; royalists divide between free-market and protective views.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Religious traditionalist royalists lean against; inferred.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Imperative mandate and constant removal contradict royalist stability; inferred.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Pension design is outside monarchist doctrine, and adherents divide along ordinary economic lines.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Land held only while used contradicts hereditary landed property; inferred.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Bodin himself resisted royal subsidy requests at the Estates of Blois and constitutional monarchies require parliamentary supply, but James VI and I treated the king as overlord of all land; the lean is to agree but strands are split.

single-official-language.rationale: Not addressed; Belgium shows multilingual crowns.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Land-ownership restrictions on foreigners are not part of monarchist doctrine, though landed royalists may be protective.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Inferred from conservative outlook; not addressed.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: The sources never address consumerism; traditionalists may agree but liberal royalists do not.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Covert arming of insurgents is not covered by monarchist sources, and adherents divide on foreign policy.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Bloc-discipline interventions of the Brezhnev-doctrine type are not addressed by monarchist sources; the Holy Alliance tradition suggests some royalists approved, but modern ones differ.

corporate-influence.rationale: Lobbying is not addressed in monarchist sources, though Feeney's argument that the crown checks populists hints at distrust of money in politics only loosely; adherents split.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Restrictions on foreign funding of NGOs are a sovereignty question not discussed by monarchist doctrine; adherents are split.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Dynastic concern with family is suggestive but doctrine is silent.

residents-only-property.rationale: Local property restrictions are not addressed in the sources and adherents differ.

job-guarantee.rationale: An employer-of-last-resort state is not part of monarchist doctrine, and royalists divide between paternalists and free-market conservatives.

democratic-peace.rationale: Democratic-peace theory is a liberal international-relations claim absent from the monarchist sources; adherents are split.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Monarchist doctrine demands loyalty and obedience to lawful authority, and Maistre treats attacks on sovereignty as among the gravest crimes.

non-intervention.rationale: The Holy Alliance tradition shows royalists intervening to defend thrones, but modern monarchism holds no unified stance, so adherents split.

industrial-unions.rationale: Union structure is a labour question outside monarchist doctrine; adherents have no common position.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Conspiracy theories are not monarchist doctrine; inferred.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Dynastic succession depends on legal marriage and legitimacy, and traditionalists defend it; inferred.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Freedom-of-information law is not addressed in monarchist sources, and royal households often resist disclosure, so adherents split.

local-production.rationale: Localism in production is not addressed in monarchist sources, and royalists hold no common view.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Monarchist sources do not address the primacy of national over international law; sovereigntist and integrationist royalists differ.

religious-nation.rationale: Faith-defined crowns (Thailand, Saudi Arabia, Japan) exist but constitutional monarchies are mostly secular; split.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Imperial Chinese tributary system is a historical monarchy practice but not a monarchist doctrine.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Regional fiscal sharing is not addressed in monarchist doctrine, though multinational crowns such as Belgium face the issue; adherents split.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: The communist distinction between personal and productive property is not a monarchist topic; royalists favour private property generally but the sources do not say so.

defeat-communism.rationale: Royalists historically opposed communism, notably restorationists and Orwell-era defenders; not a stated doctrine.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Public-service delivery models are outside monarchist doctrine, and adherents divide along ordinary party lines.

religion-illusion.rationale: Maistre argues for religion as the basis of social order and throne-and-altar, so adherents reject treating it as illusion.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Monarchist sources do not assess capitalism's historical role; traditionalists are ambivalent and liberal royalists favourable.

socialized-care.rationale: Inferred from family tradition; not addressed.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Language purism is a nationalist cause not found in monarchist sources, so adherents are split.

treaties-binding.rationale: Treaties with nations inside a state, such as the Crown's treaties with indigenous peoples, are not addressed in the sources; adherents split.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Utopian egalitarian communities contradict hierarchical monarchist order; inferred.

majority-settlement.rationale: Settlement policy toward minority regions is not addressed in the monarchist sources, and multinational crowns such as Belgium's argue against ethnic engineering, so adherents are split.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Distributist and corporatist royalists say yes, liberal royalists do not.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Historical and religious claims to land are not monarchist doctrine, though dynastic claims are common; adherents split.

holocaust-denial.rationale: A historical falsehood not part of monarchism; mainstream monarchists reject it.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Some monarchies criminalise it but modern constitutional royalists generally do not; inferred.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Constitutional monarchists defend legal opposition (monarchies replace leaders through elections, per Schleiter and Morgan-Jones), though absolutist strands suppress it.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Established-church royalists and absolutists lean yes, constitutional ones no; split.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Imperial monarchists accepted this historically but modern monarchism does not address it.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: This is a specifically Islamic legal claim not addressed in the monarchist sources, though Muslim monarchies exist; adherents split.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Monarchists support established rulers' legitimacy and reject armed removal of rulers; inferred.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Monarchists favour representative or hierarchical institutions; inferred.

assisted-dying.rationale: Religious and traditionalist royalists lean against; inferred.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Not addressed; some royalists claim to stand above the divide, others identify as right.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Monarchist doctrine has no position on Islam and Western values; Muslim monarchies exist and royalist views vary.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Bossuet calls the royal throne the throne of God, James VI and I calls kings God's lieutenants, and Ayuso binds the Carlist king to God's sovereignty; modern constitutional monarchists rarely press this, so the answer stops short of strongly agree.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Established-church monarchies tolerate religious symbols; inferred.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Employment-law rules on non-disclosure agreements are outside monarchist doctrine; adherents split.

social-market-economy.rationale: Economic systems are not addressed in the monarchist sources, though paternalist royalists would favour social protection and market liberals would not.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Constitutional monarchies treat the armed forces as owing allegiance to the Crown and none of the sources suggest abolishing them.

rich-first.rationale: Deng-style gradualist development is a Chinese reform idea not addressed in monarchist sources; adherents split.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Alliance policy is not addressed in monarchist doctrine; royalists in neutral states such as Sweden and in NATO states differ.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Hegel holds that the monarch comes to office by natural birth so that the throne is kept out of factional contest, and Ayuso makes right by birth the first condition of Carlist legitimacy.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: A doctrine about the form of the state; adherents split on economic questions (inferred).

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Economic policy is outside the doctrine, and adherents divide on it (inferred).

property-franchise.rationale: Traditional monarchists often accepted property or rank limits, but modern constitutional ones accept universal suffrage; adherents are split.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Traditionalist monarchists see the sexes as complementary, and the doctrine takes no position on ecofeminism (inferred).

reification.rationale: A Marxist critique that monarchists seldom hold; their defence of tradition favours existing orders (inferred).

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Most monarchists defend press and assembly freedoms as real, even under private ownership (inferred).

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: James VI and I says a good king governs by law and a just prince takes no life without clear law, and Bossuet distinguishes absolute from arbitrary rule, though absolutists let the king suspend laws for reasons known to him.

racial-franchise.rationale: The crown is described as a symbol of unity of all subjects, so confining politics to one race runs against it, though some historical monarchies did so.

online-participation.rationale: Anachronistic; the Crown as dignified part of government stands apart from popular deliberation (inferred).

open-government-data.rationale: Constitutional monarchies publish records, but monarchism says nothing on it and Bagehot defends some secrecy (inferred).

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Established-church monarchists have supported limits, but the modern constitutional majority supports freedom to marry; inferred.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Monarchism is about the crown as a unifier of all subjects, so shunning a religious minority runs against it (inferred).

citizens-assembly.rationale: Monarchists defend hereditary crown and representative institutions (Bagehot, Maistre) over novel devices like sortition; inferred, as the question is not addressed.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Traditional and counter-revolutionary strands keep inherited doctrine while modern constitutional monarchists are mixed; the doctrine is about the form of state and adherents split.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Monarchism is a doctrine about the form of the state and its adherents split on economic questions; inferred, no stated position.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Modern constitutional monarchists generally accept it while traditionalist strands object; adherents are split and the doctrine is silent.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Monarchist defences rest on tradition and religion beneath the crown, so state atheism is rejected; inferred from those principles.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Monarchism prizes order and continuity of authority, so abolishing police and prisons is rejected; inferred.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: The doctrine does not address consociation; a shared crown can unify communities but adherents differ on power-sharing.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Traditionalist monarchists favour local community and church over central bureaucracy; inferred and contested.

term-limits.rationale: Hereditary continuity is valued over rotation of office, so elected-office term limits are mildly disfavoured; inferred.

vote-delegation.rationale: Delegated direct voting runs against deference to stable institutions; inferred.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Monarchism says nothing on existential risk, and adherents are indifferent.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Traditionalist strands oppose, modern constitutional ones accept; adherents split.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Older strands assume a husband's headship while modern monarchists accept equal spouses; split.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Inferred: citizenship and allegiance to the crown are central, though constitutional monarchists in some countries accept local voting for residents.

rent-control.rationale: Monarchism is a doctrine of the state's form, and its adherents divide on economic policy.

abolish-ip.rationale: Inferred from the traditionalist, property-respecting majority; adherents have no stated position.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Inferred: traditional monarchists favour discipline, but organised drilled youth movements are associated with modern mass ideologies.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Adherents divide and the doctrine does not address it.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Adherents divide between sovereignty concerns and alliance loyalty; the doctrine is silent.

recognise-genocide.rationale: The doctrine is silent and adherents divide.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Adherents divide between aristocratic landed property defenders and others; no doctrine on it.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Inferred: monarchist traditions accept just war and the right of self-defence, and no strand holds an absolute ban.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Monarchists prize continuity and tradition, with the crown as a symbol of national continuity, though the claim of unbroken identity from antiquity goes beyond the sources.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Inferred from the traditionalist outlook, which holds sex to be natural and hereditary succession itself a rule about it.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Inferred from the traditionalist majority; no doctrine on feminist theory.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Inferred: monarchists generally honour those who die for crown and country, and counter-revolutionary strands venerate royal martyrs.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Divine-right and counter-revolutionary strands like Maistre's see a providential struggle, but constitutional monarchists do not.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: No doctrine; the doctrine concerns the form of the state.

culture-before-state.rationale: No doctrine on sequencing; the crown is both a cultural and a state institution.

god-not-male.rationale: Inferred from the religious traditionalism of the strands; constitutional monarchists are divided and the doctrine is silent.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Inferred from the traditionalist majority; not a doctrinal question.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: The doctrine has no position, and constitutional crowns generally stand above ethnic division.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: No doctrine; monarchies are often multi-ethnic and the crown unites several peoples.

independent-unions.rationale: Monarchism is a form-of-government doctrine with no union position; royalists range from corporatist to liberal.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Inferred: monarchists defend hereditary rule and social continuity above class, and most reject class-based claims to rule.

local-essentials-public.rationale: No position; royalist parties split between paternalist and free-market views.

second-chamber.rationale: Inferred: most constitutional monarchies keep an upper house beside the elected one, as Bagehot's English Constitution describes the Lords, though not all do.

municipal-property.rationale: Inferred: monarchists mostly defend private property and tradition, and community ownership is not part of the doctrine.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Inferred: monarchists defend a unified crown and nation, and confederal local assemblies cut against that unity.

family-wage.rationale: No position on wages; traditionalist monarchists often favour the family, but the doctrine does not address it.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Anachronistic; the doctrine says nothing on drug regulation.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Anachronistic; the doctrine says nothing on ageing research.

anonymous-payments.rationale: No position; the doctrine concerns the form of the state, and royalist views on money and privacy vary.

online-anonymity.rationale: No position; the doctrine concerns the form of the state, and royalist views on online privacy vary.

person-over-state.rationale: Constitutional monarchists defend individual liberty while counter-revolutionary ones put community and tradition first, so strands divide.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Inferred: the divine-right and counter-revolutionary strands tie the crown to religion, and the traditional case values the sacred in public life; the constitutional strand is less so.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Carlists treat regional fueros as rights the king must respect, while unitary constitutional monarchies leave devolution to parliament; the strands are split.

gm-crops.rationale: No position; royalists divide on agriculture and technology.

dense-cities.rationale: No position; royalists divide on urban and environmental questions.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Inferred: the crown is defended as a symbol of national unity above faction, which cuts against organising by racial group.

racial-pride.rationale: No position; the doctrine is about the form of the state and monarchists split on national and ancestral pride.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Constitutional monarchists generally accept defensive war as the norm but the counter-revolutionary tradition honours the martial crown, so adherents split.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Monarchism is about the form of the state; dynastic loyalty often crosses language lines, while nationalist monarchists would agree, so adherents are split.

communal-electorates.rationale: The constitutional crown is defended as a symbol of unity above sections of the nation, which tells against separate religious electorates; inferred.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Monarchism has no position on foreign plots; adherents divide by country and period.

free-public-college.rationale: Monarchism says little on economic policy and its adherents divide on it.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Monarchism is a doctrine of the form of the state; its adherents divide on environmental policy tools.

future-generations.rationale: The traditionalist and counter-revolutionary strands stress duties across generations (Maistre) and continuity of the crown; inferred for environmental stewardship.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Monarchism does not address the question and adherents divide on it.

arms-reduction.rationale: Adherents divide: constitutional monarchists back moderate defence, traditionalists keep arms as sovereigns judge fit; not a monarchist doctrine.

open-diplomacy.rationale: The traditional view is that royal and state diplomacy needs confidentiality; inferred, as modern constitutional monarchs leave it to governments.

capital-controls.rationale: Monarchism says little on economic policy and its adherents divide on it.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Monarchism has no gun policy; the crown as head of the state's armed forces (s4) implies a state monopoly on force, inferred from that.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Monarchs are commanders-in-chief and loyalty to the crown is central, so refusing orders cuts against the tradition; inferred from s4.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Monarchism is a form-of-state doctrine and royalists range from paternalist to free-market (s1), so no common view.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: No stated position; paternalist royalists might agree and free-market royalists would not (s1).

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Nothing in the doctrine addresses borrowing limits; adherents split by economic tradition (s1).

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Traditionalist and counter-revolutionary monarchists favour existing orders over redesign (s3); inferred, not stated.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Monarchists defend inherited institutions and the continuity of the state; Maistre treats overthrow as catastrophe (s3).

free-economic-experiment.rationale: The tradition prizes continuity and one unifying national order (s2, s4) over communities trying different systems; inferred.

nature-as-capital.rationale: The doctrine does not address environmental accounting; royalists are split.

sacred-nation.rationale: Bagehot treats the Crown as a religion-like symbol of national unity and Maistre ties nations to providence, though modern constitutional monarchists stop short of calling the nation sacred.

student-debt-relief.rationale: No stated position and adherents divide on fiscal questions (s1).

internal-colonialism.rationale: The crown is defended as a symbol of unity above regions and classes (s4), which tells against reading the centre as colonising its regions; inferred.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Maistre and Christian royalists hold a fixed created human nature that should not be remade (s3); inferred, as constitutional monarchists say little.

public-service-media.rationale: No doctrine on broadcasting; royalist views range from support for national broadcasters to market scepticism (s1).

religions-one-truth.rationale: Inferred from the counter-revolutionary and divine-right strands, which tie the crown to one established faith and treat rival creeds as error; Bagehot treats the Crown's religion-like aura as a national matter, not a universal one.

farm-price-support.rationale: Monarchism is a doctrine about the form of the state and says nothing on farm policy; royalists divide between paternalists and free-marketeers.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Inferred: constitutional crowns such as the British one sit at the head of states that keep their arsenals, and monarchists stress national continuity and the armed forces' loyalty to the crown.

workers-own-party.rationale: Inferred from the monarchist claim that the crown stands for national unity above party; a class party is the opposite of that, though monarchists do not address it directly.

ban-fgm.rationale: Inferred: the sources do not discuss it, but modern constitutional monarchists accept the criminal law's protection of persons, and the traditional case rests on protecting the weak under the crown.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Monarchists are split: modern crowns have equal succession, but traditional and divine-right strands defended male-line inheritance and custom; no source addresses women's land rights.

one-language-many-names.rationale: Nothing in monarchist sources addresses language naming, and adherents divide with ordinary national and regional loyalties.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: A form-of-government doctrine with no stated position; common-law property protection fits traditionalists while others accept regulation.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Inferred from the traditional case for hereditary authority; Bagehot defends the hereditary Lords as a dignified part of the constitution, which fits a recognised place for hereditary custom-holders.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Monarchists split: conservationist traditionalists favour stewardship, while others defend liberty and property; the sources do not address the trade-off.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: No source addresses sentencing, and adherents divide between order-minded traditionalists and defenders of judicial independence under the crown.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Inferred from the monarchist emphasis on a shared national tradition and the crown as symbol of national unity; requiring the language is a mild extension.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Monarchism has no labour position, and monarchists divide along ordinary left-right lines.

voter-id.rationale: Monarchism is about the form of the state, so electoral-integrity rules are not addressed; monarchists divide.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Some monarchies have an established church, others are plural; monarchists are split.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Constitutional monarchists accept elected government as legitimate, but traditional and divine-right strands root legitimacy in the crown; adherents are split.

premarital-sex.rationale: Modern constitutional monarchists vary and traditional ones are conservative; adherents are split.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Constitutional monarchists generally accept liberal civil rights, though traditionalists would favour order; inferred and low.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Monarchism has no economic programme and its adherents range from paternalist to free-market.

women-suffrage.rationale: Modern monarchies, including constitutional ones, give women equal vote and office, with female monarchs accepted; older strands differ.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Many monarchists value religion and tradition, so they would mostly reject the claim; inferred.

race-social-construct.rationale: Monarchism takes no position on race, and adherents divide.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Monarchism has no position on gender-equality bodies, and monarchists divide.

homestead-ownership.rationale: Monarchism is about the form of the state; adherents split on property theories.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: Adherents are split between sovereignty-minded traditionalists and constitutional monarchists comfortable with international law.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Split: the divine-right strand accepts scripture's authority, while constitutional monarchists take no position.

gendered-self-government.rationale: Monarchism is silent on this and adherents divide on it.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Inferred: the doctrine says nothing on planned economies, but adherents' tradition and property conservatism lean against it.

indirect-election.rationale: Adherents differ; the doctrine concerns the head of state, not how higher offices are filled.

national-church-status.rationale: Maistre defended an established Catholic church, Carlists made Catholic unity a pillar of the monarchy, and constitutional crowns often head or uphold a national faith.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Adherents are split; the doctrine does not address regional autonomy.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Inferred: monarchists tend to rest legitimacy on tradition and dynastic continuity rather than popular votes.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: Anachronistic or unaddressed; adherents are split.

simple-living.rationale: Not addressed by the doctrine; adherents are split.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: Not addressed by the doctrine; adherents are split.

equal-conscription.rationale: Not addressed by the doctrine; adherents are split.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: Maistre's providential view of France and Maurras's nation-first royalism point to a sacred tie to the land of the ancestors, but this is drawn from their wider views rather than stated.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: James VI and I says a just prince will not take a subject's life without a clear law, and Bossuet separates absolute from arbitrary power; constitutional monarchists defend the rule of law.

close-ties-china.rationale: Monarchism as a doctrine about the form of the state takes no position on alignment with China or the United States.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: Monarchist sources say nothing about co-nationals abroad; multinational crowns like the Habsburgs cut across nations, so no clear lean.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: The view that appropriators owe compensation to all is foreign to Filmer's and James's derivation of property from the ruler and to Kuehnelt-Leddihn's defence of property; low as no source discusses it.

self-ownership.rationale: Filmer denies that people are born free of subjection, which tells against full self-ownership; modern constitutional monarchists take no distinctive view, so this is low.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: Monarchism has no doctrine on consumption taxes; adherents follow various economic programmes.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: Monarchist sources do not address how welfare should be targeted, and adherents hold a range of economic views.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Maurras blames parties and parliament for national weakness, while constitutional monarchists defend party parliaments under a neutral Crown; the strands are split.

no-business-privileges.rationale: Monarchism takes no stand on business privileges; royal charters and monopolies were common under historic crowns, while modern monarchists follow their parties.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: Confessional Carlists and Catholic legitimists organise around a faith while constitutional monarchists usually do not, so the strands are split.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: Monarchists keep an ancestral institution within modern states, as Hegel's modern constitutional monarchy shows, but no source frames it this way, so low.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: Monarchist sources say nothing about divorce law; traditionalist Catholic royalists would oppose easy divorce while constitutional monarchists vary.

national-resource-control.rationale: Bodin resisted alienating crown lands and Maurras put national interest first; low because neither addresses natural resources as such.

distribution-by-process.rationale: Monarchism is a doctrine about the form of the state and takes no position on distributive justice; royalist strands range from paternalist to free-market.

financial-transactions-tax.rationale: Monarchism does not address financial taxation, and strands differ on economic policy.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: Monarchism does not address racial inequality, so no stated position exists and strands differ.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: James VI and I and Filmer deny any right of resistance and treat the king's law as binding, but Maistre's Catholic strand accepts higher law; a weak lean inferred from the absolutist texts.

automate-paid-work.rationale: Monarchism is silent on automation and work; inferred neutral.

multipolar-world.rationale: Counter-revolutionary monarchists favoured a concert of crowned powers, but constitutional monarchists differ and none state a view of world order.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: Monarchism has no position on the theory of value; neutral.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Maurras's Action française ties nationalism to monarchy, and the monarchist leagues stress the crown as national unity; the 'working people' part is not addressed, so inferred.

material-over-identity.rationale: Monarchism is not a left-wing doctrine and does not address this internal left debate.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: Monarchists, such as the Carlists, are anti-communist and defend throne and altar; a party-led socialist system is inferred to be rejected, but the issue is not addressed.

notes: Re-audit of a thin four-source profile. The absolutist strand (Bodin, Filmer, James, Bossuet) and the constitutional strand (Bagehot, Hegel, monarchist leagues) answer differently on sovereign-above-law, parliament-supreme, resist-lawless-ruler, democracy-best, separated-powers, mixed-constitution and budget-needs-parliament; these are 0 or weak leans at low confidence. Traditionalists (Maurras, Carlists) add decentralisation and organic representation that constitutional monarchists do not share. Maurras's monarchism was bound up with integral nationalism and antisemitism (s13); that is a feature of his strand, not of monarchism generally. The three missing statements of the earlier audit have already been added to the bank (monarchy-legitimate, nonpartisan-head-of-state).
